Preparing a comprehensive answer covering every distinct memo visibility enforcement site across production server surfaces.

Five distinct enforcement sites identified so far. API helpers `checkMemoReadAccess` and `checkAttachmentAccess` guard memo and attachment reads. `checkAttachmentPermission` in the fileserver layer covers share tokens. `SSEClient.canReceive` restricts SSE broadcasts. `GetMemo` invokes the API helper directly.

Seven additional enforcement sites found. `ListMemos` applies `VisibilityList` and a CEL filter. `ListMemoComments` uses `checkMemoReadAccess` and `MemoFilter`. `ListMemoRelations` applies `MemoFilter`. `ListMemoAttachments` uses inline checks. `GetAttachment` invokes `checkAttachmentAccess`. `ListMemoReactions` and `UpsertMemoReaction` rely on inline guards.

`GetMemoByShare` enforces share-token access in `memo_share_service.go` lines 153–166. `GetUserStats` and `ListAllUserStats` apply `VisibilityList` in `user_service_stats.go` lines 217–221 and 83–91. `batchConvertMemoRelations` filters related memo snippets via `MemoFilter` in `memo_service_converter.go` lines 182–206. `ListMemos` also applies `VisibilityList` SQL directly in the Postgres, SQLite, and MySQL query files.

RSS explore and user feeds enforce visibility in `rss.go` lines 88–93 and 138–144. The frontend sitemap in `frontend.go` lines 149–151 also gates access. Fileserver attachment, thumbnail, and motion endpoints route through `fileserver.go` line 149 into `checkAttachmentPermission`. SSE broadcast filtering in `sse_hub.go` lines 115–131 relies on `canReceive`. Frontend SPA serving, link metadata resolution, and MCP delegation are excluded because they do not enforce memo visibility server-side.

`ListAttachments` only allows a user’s own attachments. `UpdateMemo` and `CreateMemo` handle visibility mutation and serialization. `sse_event_helpECreatorID` provides metadata for filtering rather than enforcing access. Notification and mention helpers are outbound traffic and do not gate viewing. A distinct enforcement site is a separately reachable code path that performs its own allow/deny or row-filtering before exposing memo text, attachment bytes, relation or comment snippets, stats, or live refresh signals.

Centralized helpers reused across RPCs are treated as a single shared implementation. SQL `VisibilityList` and `MemoFilter` compilation in the store layer is a separate site invoked by many handlers. Inline enforcement logic duplicated inside `reaction_service.go` and `memo_attachment_service.go` counts as distinct sites because those handlers do not call the centralized helper.

ListMemoRelations does not call checkMemoReadAccess on the anchor memo. This may be a gap. The user asked for existing enforcement sites. That distinction matters.

CreateMemoComment at line 41 gates comment creation. It checks parent memo visibility before writing. This is a write-side gate. It is borderline for viewing enforcement. It will be noted briefly.
